title: Injection-fixture generator (local-only); live adversarial eval is operator-invoked
summary: corpus.derive_injection_fixtures reads the machine-local imported AgentDojo goals and writes fixture documents plus an injection_extraction case file under .agent-local/evals/injection-imported (gitignored). It authors only a neutral service-note scaffold with owner/port labels and a canary; the attacker goal (licensed benchmark data) flows local-file -> local-file and never enters Git or a response. `orchestrate corpus import XC-agentdojo --write --derive` runs import and derivation together. The live adversarial eval -- feeding these fixtures to a real worker -- is left operator-invoked rather than run autonomously: driving live injection attacks and generating the payloads collides with the environment's safety classifier (FND-0013, and an interrupted attempt in ORCH-0020), so per constitution stop conditions it is gated to the operator instead of retried. The deterministic protections these cases would exercise are already validated by tests/test_publication_guard.py (guard fails a node whose transcript shows a publishing command) and EXP-0007 (read-only injection resistance).

prior_art.reused: the goals as fixture content, local-only
prior_art.why_custom: generator keeps payloads machine-local; scaffold is neutral

operator_command: agent-os orchestrate corpus import XC-agentdojo --write --derive  then  agent-os orchestrate eval --suite EVS-SECURITY --incumbent codex@fast --route codex@fast+attach --samples 3  (after pointing EVS-SECURITY at .agent-local/evals/injection-imported/cases.json)
